title: N-Queens II
statement_short: The n-queens puzzle is the problem of placing n queens on an n x n chessboard such that no two queens attack each other. Given an integer n, return the number of distinct solutions to the n-queens puzzle.
hint: Extremely small board dimension (n <= 9) allows recursive row-by-row placement with diagonal conflict checks.
keywords: no two queens attack each other
why_not: Right: Backtracking places queens row by row, pruning invalid column and diagonal placements in O(n!) time. Not Bit Manipulation: Bitmasks optimize conflict checking speed, but the core placement algorithm is backtracking search. Not 2D DP: Grid state caching fails because queen attack paths depend on global column and diagonal constraints. Not Graph DFS: DFS explores graph vertices, but N-Queens placement relies on row-level branch pruning.
